structured_output.summary: Phase 13 is a planning/governance phase and its acceptance criteria are met with real, executed evidence. docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md pins an unambiguous release scope (accepted source 167a359, version 0.2.0, owner cdot65, tag v0.2.0, MSRV 1.89, both compilers, deferred Portkey/Gateway commit) and every factual claim I sampled verifies against repository artifacts: phase-12.json contains exactly 39 passing checks at source de311207…, docs/checks/phase-12-remote-ci-run-19.json records run 19 success with 47/47 jobs at commit 167a359, CHANGELOG.md:34-48 lists exactly twelve option rejections, CHANGELOG.md:56-59 records exactly four response-presence waivers, contracts/response-defaults.json:18 records 23 default bindings, and crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:3 is already 0.2.0 (so the "no manifest change" guard and the publish target do not contradict). docs/checks/phase-13.json is a genuinely executed report: five checks, all exit_code 0, source_unchanged true, source_sha256 07c089e5… matching the reviewed source, and its command list is byte-identical to check_phase.commands_for(13) (tools/check_phase.py:71-74), so review_phase.check_evidence would accept it. tools/test_release_020.py adds a real (not prose) guard that the runtime/packaged paths are unchanged versus the accepted commit, that the seven previously accepted command sets still equal their recorded reports, and that phase sequencing goes 13→14 without reopening the completed 90–92 maintenance track; predecessor gates stay enforced by review_phase.validate_predecessors. Publication controls in the plan are strong: verify-before-act on an existing version, no overwrite/yank, registry read on ambiguous results, repackage-and-SHA-match before `--no-verify` publish backed by scripts/check-package.py --require-clean (which genuinely extracts the archive and runs minimal/all-feature unit tests, example checks, doctests and the external consumer), and post-publish verification of the downloaded artifact against both compiler proofs. No blocker or high finding. The residual gaps are scope/documentation completeness rather than correctness: the packaged README.md is omitted from the byte-for-byte guard while documentation is explicitly allowed to change; the four retained phase-12 review advisories (including a user-facing docs/RED_TEAM.md defect that 0.2.0 ships) have no disposition in the release plan; and the release plan itself is not reachable from docs/PHASES.md or docs/implementation-plan.md, which AGENTS.md makes mandatory reading.

findings.description: README.md is a packaged payload file (crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml:10-11 sets readme and include = ["src/**", "examples/**", "LICENSE", "NOTICE", "README.md"]; docs/checks/phase-12-package-1.99.0.json:54-56 shows README.md at 5,581 bytes inside the archive). The fixed scope at line 16 promises to "Compare all runtime inputs byte-for-byte to the accepted source and fail on drift", and the phase-14 candidate guard at lines 45-47 enumerates only source/example bytes, legal notice, crate/workspace manifests and the lockfile, while line 47 and step 1 explicitly permit documentation (including "public install guidance") to change. The executed guard has the same hole: tools/test_release_020.py:27-28 compares Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE, crates/scm-sdk/Cargo.toml, crates/scm-sdk/src and crates/scm-sdk/examples and omits README.md. A README edit therefore changes the published archive bytes while the plan's "unchanged SDK proof" guard still reports no drift.
findings.required_fix: Add README.md to the compared path set in tools/test_release_020.py:27-28 and to the enumerated phase-14 candidate guard in docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md:45-47, or state explicitly in the plan that README.md is a packaged file whose permitted documentation changes alter the archive and that both clean-archive proofs must be regenerated after any README edit.

findings.description: The plan does not dispose of the four nonblocking advisories retained from the accepted phase-12 review (docs/phase-status.json:2217-2253), even though all four are documentation/tooling items that line 47 permits to change. The medium one is user-facing and ships with 0.2.0: docs/RED_TEAM.md:94-111 still states "Direct list calls omit unspecified `skip`, `limit`, and `search` fields" and never says that the twelve bindings in CHANGELOG.md:34-48 now fail validation before authentication on their specific methods, nor links the migration table from that section. 0.2.0 is exactly the release in which that behavior becomes consumer-visible, so the release plan should decide whether the reconciliation lands before publication or is deferred.
findings.required_fix: Add an explicit disposition in docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md for each of the four retained phase-12 advisories (docs/phase-status.json:2217-2253) — either scheduled in the phase-14 release-documentation step or recorded as post-0.2.0 maintenance — and in particular state whether the docs/RED_TEAM.md:94-111 pagination/request-constraints reconciliation and CHANGELOG migration link are required before publishing 0.2.0.

findings.description: The authorized 0.2.0 release procedure is not reachable from the two documents AGENTS.md:3 makes mandatory reading. docs/PHASES.md adds rows 13 and 14 (lines 23-24) but never references docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md, unlike the vendor track (lines 63-71 point at docs/red-team-data-plane-0.93.0-plan.md) and the maintenance track (lines 29-30 point at docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md); the "Milestone records" checklist (lines 39-50) also stops at item 12. docs/implementation-plan.md:127 still authorizes only "the authorized 0.1.1 maintenance procedure ... in docs/g10-0.1.1-plan.md", so the publication contract there records no 0.2.0 authorization. The plan is currently referenced only from docs/phase-status.json:2275 and 2993.
findings.required_fix: Add a short "SDK 0.2.0 release" section (or an inline link on docs/PHASES.md:23-24) pointing at docs/release-0.2.0-plan.md with milestone entries 13 and 14, and record the authorized 0.2.0 publication procedure and its plan path in docs/implementation-plan.md:127 alongside the existing 0.1.1 sentence.

findings.description: The no-change guard uses `git diff --name-only <baseline> -- <paths>`, which reports only tracked differences. A newly added, still-untracked file under crates/scm-sdk/src or crates/scm-sdk/examples would be packaged by cargo (Cargo.toml include globs) yet pass this assertion, and the phase-13 command set (tools/check_phase.py:72) runs only `git diff --check`, which likewise ignores untracked files. The window closes only at phase-14 step 3, where scripts/check-package.py:108-110 requires a clean tree including untracked files.
